lad-agent.prompt: Put the agent's lifecycle in the order it must happen.
lad-agent.steps[0].label: Define the agent: PromptAgentDefinition(model=MODEL_NAME, instructions=..., tools=[...])
lad-agent.steps[0].detail: Model + instructions + tools set at definition time — {"deployment":{"model":AGENT_NAME}} is the canonical wrong answer; deployments host models, agents are model + instructions + tools.
lad-agent.steps[1].label: Test it in the Agents playground
lad-agent.steps[1].detail: The playground configures persona, tools, and attached knowledge side by side and lets you try multi-turn behavior before any client code calls the agent.
lad-agent.steps[2].label: Save it: project.agents.create_version(...) — pass the agent_name plus the definition
lad-agent.steps[2].detail: Unsaved playground edits are lost on leaving the portal — create_version is what actually persists a definition, whether you built it in the portal or in code.
lad-agent.steps[3].label: Create a thread: openai.conversations.create()
lad-agent.steps[3].detail: Opens the runtime container that later turns write into — called by the client app before the first message is sent, distinct from the agent's own definition.
lad-agent.steps[4].label: Add the user's message to the thread
lad-agent.steps[4].detail: The turn's content is appended to the thread's accumulating message history — a run can't process a message that hasn't been added yet.
lad-agent.steps[5].label: Create a run and read the output: openai.responses.create(..., extra_body={"agent_reference": {...}})
lad-agent.steps[5].detail: The invocation that actually processes the conversation and produces the agent's next output; agent_reference is per-call metadata pointing at the saved definition.

lad-chat.prompt: Put the code flow in the order it must run.
lad-chat.steps[0].label: Install azure-ai-projects
lad-chat.steps[0].detail: The Foundry project client ships in the azure-ai-projects package — expect questions that ask you to name it.
lad-chat.steps[1].label: Create AIProjectClient(endpoint, DefaultAzureCredential())
lad-chat.steps[1].detail: Endpoint + credential must both exist before any call; keyless auth = Entra ID DefaultAzureCredential.
lad-chat.steps[2].label: Call get_openai_client()
lad-chat.steps[2].detail: Bridges the project client to an OpenAI-compatible chat client — the line that breaks everything if removed.
lad-chat.steps[3].label: Build the messages list (system prompt first, then user prompt)
lad-chat.steps[3].detail: Rules and guardrails in the system message; this turn's request in the user message.
lad-chat.steps[4].label: Call chat.completions.create(model=DEPLOYMENT_NAME, messages=[...])
lad-chat.steps[4].detail: model= takes YOUR deployment name, never the base model name — the classic trap.
lad-chat.steps[5].label: Read response.choices[0].message.content
lad-chat.steps[5].detail: The reply text lives on the first choice's message — corpus snippet questions end here.

lad-cu.prompt: Put the Content Understanding workflow in order.
lad-cu.steps[0].label: Choose or define an analyzer: describe the schema in natural language (ContentAnalyzer(base_analyzer_id=..., field_schema=...))
lad-cu.steps[0].detail: Prebuilt analyzer ids (prebuilt-invoice, prebuilt-audio,...) cover common domains; a custom ContentAnalyzer names the fields you want in plain language via field_schema — no code beyond describing what to extract.
lad-cu.steps[1].label: Register it: client.begin_create_analyzer(...)
lad-cu.steps[1].detail: Provisions the analyzer definition as a long-running operation before it can be called against any content — a one-time setup step, not a per-document one.
lad-cu.steps[2].label: Submit each file: call begin_analyze on the client, naming the analyzer's id and wrapping the file URL in an AnalysisInput
lad-cu.steps[2].detail: Each document/image/audio/video file gets its own begin_analyze call against the already-registered analyzer — the per-document step, unlike step 2.
lad-cu.steps[3].label: Poll the operation: poller.result()
lad-cu.steps[3].detail: begin_analyze hands back a poller rather than the finished result; calling .result() on it blocks until the long-running analysis completes — the work is asynchronous, so expect to be asked which poller method retrieves the outcome.
lad-cu.steps[4].label: Read the structured JSON fields from the result
lad-cu.steps[4].detail: The extracted fields — vendor name, invoice date, invoice total, and the like — land in the poller's result payload; this is where Content Understanding's own job ends.
lad-cu.steps[5].label: Hand off to Azure AI Search for indexing
lad-cu.steps[5].detail: Content Understanding only extracts — it never indexes or generates; Azure AI Search is the separate downstream service that indexes CU's structured output for retrieval/RAG.

lad-genai.prompt: Put the steps in the order a generative model turns your prompt into text.
lad-genai.steps[0].label: Tokenization
lad-genai.steps[0].detail: Input text is split into tokens — words or sub-words — each mapped to an id from the model's vocabulary; nothing downstream has meaning until this happens (Task 1.2).
lad-genai.steps[1].label: Embeddings
lad-genai.steps[1].detail: Each token id is converted into a numeric vector encoding meaning — the same vector space that makes semantic similarity computable as vector distance.
lad-genai.steps[2].label: Transformer attention
lad-genai.steps[2].detail: Self-attention layers weigh every token against every other token in the sequence — the mechanic that 'powers most modern foundation models,' and it needs the embedding vectors to already exist.
lad-genai.steps[3].label: Next-token prediction
lad-genai.steps[3].detail: The model outputs a probability distribution over the whole vocabulary for the single next token; temperature and top-p reshape this distribution before one token is sampled.
lad-genai.steps[4].label: Detokenized output
lad-genai.steps[4].detail: The predicted token id is decoded back to text and the loop repeats one token at a time until a stop condition — perplexity measures how well this step's predictions matched held-out text.

lad-speech.prompt: Put the Speech SDK calls in the order they must run.
lad-speech.steps[0].label: SpeechConfig(subscription=key, region=region)
lad-speech.steps[0].detail: Every Speech SDK flow starts here — the key/region (or endpoint) pair that authenticates every call that follows.
lad-speech.steps[1].label: Set speech_config.speech_synthesis_voice_name = "..."
lad-speech.steps[1].detail: Voice selection is a property set directly on the config object — exam's DragonHD-voice snippet sets this line right after SpeechConfig, before any other object is built from it.
lad-speech.steps[2].label: AudioConfig(...) — microphone, file, or default device
lad-speech.steps[2].detail: Built independently of the voice-name property, but quickstart snippets construct it only after config setup is finished, immediately before the recognizer/synthesizer that will consume both objects.
lad-speech.steps[3].label: Build the worker object — a SpeechRecognizer takes both config objects, a SpeechSynthesizer only the speech one
lad-speech.steps[3].detail: Both constructors take the already-built speech_config (the recognizer also takes audio_config) — nothing after this point can still inject the config.
lad-speech.steps[4].label: Call recognize_once() / speak_text_async(text)
lad-speech.steps[4].detail: recognize_once() captures one short utterance (vs. continuous recognition); speak_text_async() actually plays the text — the async future/.get() pattern belongs here, last, once the object exists.

lad-voice.prompt: Put the classic voice-agent pipeline in order.
lad-voice.steps[0].label: Speech-to-text: convert the caller's spoken audio into text
lad-voice.steps[0].detail: Pipeline step one — recognize_once() or continuous recognition turns audio into a transcript before any reasoning can happen on it.
lad-voice.steps[1].label: Language / generative-AI processing: reason over the transcript and produce a text reply
lad-voice.steps[1].detail: A chat/agent call reasons over the transcript — the step a single multimodal model (e.g. audio-in/audio-out chat deployment) can collapse together with steps 1 and 3, and the one the Voice Live API is built to replace all three of at once with a single low-latency speech-to-speech interface.
lad-voice.steps[2].label: Text-to-speech: synthesize the reply back to audio
lad-voice.steps[2].detail: speak_text_async() plays the generated reply — the classic pipeline's final step, also foldable into the single-multimodal-model or Voice Live alternative named in step 2's detail.
